messages:
maya: Heads-up — our Dedicated fleet canary in us-west-2 that upgraded drivers + CUDA to nvidia-driver 536 / CUDA 12.2 is showing slow AVX kernel stalls on some p3d instances. Seen on 3 nodes so far. :frowning:

jonah: saw that alert too. Which workloads are failing? any OOMs or just latency spikes? :eyes:

maya: Mostly generation latency spikes and some torch backend repro warnings. No OOMs. repro snippet from one host attached.

maya: ```
kernel: nvidia 536.16 loaded
CUDA version: 12.2
nvidia-smi: processes: python (pid 2341)
perf top shows stalls in nv_jit_kernel and ncclAllReduce_rank0
```

kevin: deploy-bot shows canary rollout started ~1746000000 for pool dedicated-us-west2-gpu-a. Canary traffic was 2% with reserved capacity.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout job 92581 started by infra-automation. Target: nvidia-driver 536 + CUDA12.2 on dedicated-us-west2-gpu-a (3 nodes).

carol: any kernel module mismatches? We recently updated a kernel package on those hosts to 6.1.22-rt. Could be interaction with driver 536.

jonah: possible. NCCL versions can be sensitive. Are we using system NCCL or the one packaged with the container images?

maya: Containers ship NCCL 2.20.3. Host has libnccl from driver 536. There's a mix. Repro logs show both libnccl.so.2 and bundled libnccl.so being loaded.

kevin: that's a red flag. For past rollouts we pinned the container NCCL or used driver-provided one exclusively. Did canary config change?

maya: Canary config included a new kernel and driver together to test upstream perf. Might've been too many changes at once.

sre-oncall: Proposal: pause the rollout, evict canary nodes from routing, and roll back driver 536 -> 532 on those 3 nodes. Also run a quick A/B comparing host-nccl vs container-nccl on identical model load.

jonah: Agreed. Steps I can take now: 1) remove canary nodes from LB 2) trigger rollback playbook 3) collect dkms/kernel module logs and ldd of libnccl from user container.

maya: removing nodes from LB now. Doing `kubectl annotate node n-dedicated-124 evict=canary-536 && kubectl cordon n-dedicated-124`

carol: I'll prepare rollback CR with driver 532 packages and kernel module rebuild. Note: rolling driver back requires reboot of GPU hosts. Need maintenance window 10–15m per node.

kevin: For rollback ordering, let's do one host at a time across AZs to avoid capacity cliffs. We have spare idle capacity in dedicated-us-west2-b (2 nodes). Use them for temporary scheduling.

maya: On it. I'll queue node 124 for rollback. Jonah — can you run quick job to test host-nccl vs container-nccl on a small 8k token gen? Use same seed.

jonah: Running now. Command I'll use:

```bash
# inside repro container
python run_infer.py --model rlhf-small --tokens 8000 --profile
ldd $(python -c 'import ctypes, os;print(ctypes.util.find_library("nccl"))')
```

maya: Test shows container-nccl path reduced tail latency by ~35% vs host libnccl on that single run. Not definitive but consistent across two runs.

carol: That suggests symbol or ABI incompat. We'll standardize on the container-bundled NCCL for now and add LD_PRELOAD/LD_LIBRARY_PATH in the canary pods as a stopgap patch during the rollback.

kevin: Good mitigation. Action items: (1) Pause canary (maya) DONE, (2) Cordon + evict nodes (maya) IN PROGRESS, (3) Rollback driver on cordoned nodes (carol) PENDING, (4) Add container-level NCCL pin for canary pods (jonah) PENDING, (5) Run regression test across 5 workloads and confirm (jonah/maya) PENDING.

deploy-bot: Canary rollback initiated: job 92581 -> rollback job 92581-rb1 by carol.

jonah: After patching LD_LIBRARY_PATH, tail latencies returned to baseline on the two test runs. We should still do the full 5-workload sweep before uncordoning nodes.

carol: Rolling node n-dedicated-124 back to driver 532 now. ETA ~12m (includes reboot). Will post logs once complete.

maya: Thanks. Also putting a note in the runbook: dont ship driver+kernel+bundled-nccl changes together in single canary. Separate them and run container compatibility check.

kevin: Agreed. We'll update rollout playbooks to require explicit NCCL sourcing check and add an automated ldd check as part of canary health.

maya: Marking this thread resolved once all 3 canary nodes are validated. Will follow up with post-mortem bullet of root cause (abi mix) and preventative changes. :thumbsup:

carol: node rollback complete. driver 532 restored, kernel module rebuilt, reboot ok. Attaching syslog excerpt: ```kernel: nvidia 532.45 loaded, no jit stalls observed```

jonah: Running full sweep now. If green I'll uncordon nodes and restart canary with smaller blast (1 node) and explicit container-nccl pin.

maya: Thanks team — great coordination.
